\begin{example} \end{example}[The Orthogonal Group]

1. ch7:7.27The orthogonal group $\mathrm O(n)=\{ A\in \mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb R):A^TA=I_n\} $ consists of matrices preserving the Euclidean inner product. The map $\Phi (A)=A^TA$ is equivariant for right multiplication on $\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb R)$ and $X\cdot B=B^TXB$ on matrices, so $\mathrm O(n)=\Phi ^{-1}(I_n)$ is a properly embedded Lie subgroup. At $I_n$, $d\Phi _{I_n}(B)=B^T+B$, whose image is the space of symmetric matrices of dimension $n(n+1)/2$; hence $\dim \mathrm O(n)=n(n-1)/2$. Every $A\in \mathrm O(n)$ has orthonormal columns and Frobenius norm $\lvert A\rvert =\sqrt n$, so the subgroup is compact as closed and bounded. \end{example}
